just_intervals.note: measured octave minus 1200 ¢, register to register

progression.narrative: The performance opens on F3 and dwells most on C in Bahr-e Nur. The line peaks at C4 (256.5 Hz) at 0:28.6. It closes on C4, not the tonic (F3 → G3 → G3 → G3 → F3 → C4).

flags: tonic F set in the catalog (the Rast-Panjgah suite's finalis F: Daramad II and ten gushe-ha end on it; read from it the suite has Rast's leading tone (the 2nd below, 4% of played time), which the other candidate, its 5th C, lacks (0.3%); Farhat 1990, pp. 100-101. Borumand's Nava on the same volume sits a tone above it, as in Farhat's keys; the vote picked the 5th. Inference, not yet by ear); the runs' vote favoured 257.3 Hz (C)
